Given the AWS FSx for NetApp ONTAP storage, this could also indicate storage-level corruption or network communication issues.
remediation: Restart the SQL Server Full-Text Filter Daemon Host service to clear any temporary corruption in the fdhost.exe process
Run DBCC CHECKDB on databases with full-text indexes to identify and repair any underlying database corruption
Check AWS FSx for NetApp ONTAP storage health and performance metrics through CloudWatch for any I/O errors or latency spikes
Verify network connectivity between SQL Server and AWS FSx storage by monitoring network latency and packet loss
Rebuild affected full-text indexes using ALTER FULLTEXT INDEX REBUILD to restore proper indexing functionality
Review Windows Event Logs and SQL Server Error Logs for additional fdhost.exe or storage-related error messages
Consider temporarily disabling full-text indexing on problematic catalogs until underlying storage issues are resolved

remediationRecommendation.error: Resource governor reconfiguration encountered an issue (HRESULT code : 0x80070002, reason: Construction of Launchpad Connection failed), while sending active external resource pool ids to launchpad. This will not fail reconfigure.
remediationRecommendation.cause: The SQL Server Launchpad service is not running or not properly configured. HRESULT 0x80070002 indicates 'The system cannot find the file specified', which typically occurs when the Launchpad service required for external script execution (R/Python) is unavailable or misconfigured. This affects Resource Governor's ability to manage external resource pools but does not prevent SQL Server from starting.
remediation: Check if SQL Server Launchpad service is installed and running using services.msc or PowerShell Get-Service command
Verify that Machine Learning Services feature is properly installed during SQL Server setup if external script execution is required
Ensure the Launchpad service account has appropriate permissions to access SQL Server and system resources
If external script execution (R/Python) is not needed, consider disabling external scripts using sp_configure 'external scripts enabled', 0
Review SQL Server error logs for additional Launchpad service startup failures or permission issues
Restart SQL Server Launchpad service after verifying service account permissions and configuration

remediationRecommendation.cause: Invalid object name referenced in query. This error occurs when a SQL query references a table, view, or other database object that does not exist in the current database context, or when the user does not have permission to access the object.
remediation: Verify that the table or object name is spelled correctly in the query
Check that the object exists in the current database using SELECT * FROM sys.tables WHERE name = 'ObjectName'
Ensure you are connected to the correct database context
Verify that the user has appropriate SELECT permissions on the referenced object
If the object should exist, check if it was dropped or renamed recently

remediationRecommendation.cause: The operating system returned error 21 (The device is not ready) to SQL Server during a read at offset in file. This is a critical I/O error indicating hardware failure, corrupted storage, or severe connectivity issues with the underlying storage system. Given that this system uses AWS FSx for NetApp ONTAP, this could indicate storage subsystem failures or network connectivity issues.
remediation: Immediately check AWS FSx for NetApp ONTAP storage health and performance metrics for any reported failures
Verify network connectivity to AWS FSx storage and check for any network interruptions or latency issues
Run DBCC CHECKDB immediately to assess the extent of potential database corruption
Check Windows Event Logs and AWS CloudWatch logs for storage-related errors or hardware failures
Consider failing over to a secondary replica if using Always On Availability Groups to maintain service availability
Contact AWS support to investigate potential FSx storage subsystem issues
Restore affected databases from clean backups if corruption is detected and cannot be repaired
Implement immediate monitoring of storage I/O performance to detect future occurrences
